content.value_statement: UI components often fail when content, states, or container sizes differ from the expected path. This skill builds a focused harness that exposes visible failures.
actual_capabilities: Reads one component to identify variable props, slots, states, and rendered data.
Selects relevant scenarios for content length, content shape, quantity, container width, state, and environment.
Builds a temporary page that imports the real component and renders each selected scenario.
Uses fixture props instead of production state or live data.
Records only visible failures and assigns each failure to a relevant domain skill.
Leaves the report page available until the user requests removal.
limitations: Tests one component per run, not complete pages or multi-component flows.
Does not diagnose failures through instrumentation, browser debugging, or repeated automated passes.
Does not modify the component or fix detected issues unless the user requests a fix.
Requires the user to inspect the report when no browser is already available.

use_cases.title: Validate a New Component
use_cases.description: Render a new component with realistic text, quantity, width, and state variations before review.

use_cases.title: Review Design System Resilience
use_cases.description: Check a shared component against narrow containers, long content, RTL text, and supported modes.

use_cases.title: Reproduce a UI Failure
use_cases.description: Isolate a reported component issue on a temporary page and compare related edge cases.

prompt_templates.title: Test One Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Stress-test the [component name] component. Build a temporary harness with relevant scenarios and report only visible failures.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a focused component check

prompt_templates.title: Test Content Resilience
prompt_templates.prompt: Test [component name] with empty, typical, long, unbreakable, RTL, and mixed-direction content where its props support these cases.

prompt_templates.title: Test States and Containers
prompt_templates.prompt: Render [component name] across supported loading, error, and disabled states within narrow, constrained, full-width, and wide containers.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Targeted Stress Matrix
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect [component path], derive applicable scenario axes from its API, explain excluded axes, build the harness, and classify observed failures by owner.

output: Long unbreakable title: text crosses the card boundary. Owner: typography.
Narrow container: action button escapes the card. Owner: layout.

output_examples.input: Test the status badge across relevant scenarios.
output_examples.output: Everything survived. The report page includes empty, typical, long, RTL, narrow-container, and disabled scenarios.

output_examples.input: Check the results list with realistic quantities and states.
output: Zero items: the list region is blank without an empty-state message. Owner: writing.
Large quantity: the list extends without the expected scroll boundary. Owner: layout.

best_practices: Choose one component and state its input, output, and intended location before building the harness.
Include only scenario axes supported by the component API, and explain why other axes were excluded.
Use the real component, application styles, fixture data, and fixed containers without adding custom presentation.
anti_patterns: Do not test every scenario axis when the component cannot receive that variation.
Do not report predicted failures that were not visible on the rendered page.
Do not connect the harness to production state, live data, or production imports.

faq.question: What does this skill test?
faq.answer: It tests one UI component against relevant content, quantity, container, state, and environment scenarios.

faq.question: Does it test complete pages?
faq.answer: No. Select one component per run so each scenario and visible failure remains clear.

faq.question: Will it change my component?
faq.answer: No. It imports the real component into a temporary harness and changes only fixture props and containers.

faq.question: Does it use production data?
faq.answer: No. The harness uses fixture data and must not import production state or connect to live data.

faq.question: Will it fix detected problems?
faq.answer: No. It reports visible failures and identifies the appropriate domain owner unless you separately request a fix.

faq.question: When is the temporary page removed?
faq.answer: The page remains available for review until you confirm that it and its fixtures can be deleted.
